run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-16T17:05:17Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate alert for otel-demo/frontend-proxy is driven by HTTP 504 responses that frontend-proxy's 'ingress' spans record after ~15.0 s of waiting on its upstream, the frontend service. The only frontend route that degraded is the recommendations path: frontend's own span p95 for 'GET /api/recommendations', 'executing api route (pages) /api/recommendations' and the client span 'grpc.oteldemo.RecommendationService/ListRecommendations' climbed from ~330 ms (16:50-17:02) to 1.47 s (17:04), 8.6 s (17:06), 13.1 s (17:08) and a flat 15 s from 17:10 on, while GET /, GET /api/cart, GET /api/data, GET /api/products/{productId}, POST /api/cart and POST /api/checkout stayed at baseline. The stall sits in the recommendation service: its own server span count (and that of its internal get_product_list span) falls from ~229 per 5 min (17:05) to 27.8 (17:07) and 0 from 17:09 onward while the frontend keeps calling at ~190-275 spans per 5 min, and its container is pinned at its 100m CPU limit with a CFS throttling ratio of 24% (17:03), 65% (17:05) and 96-99.6% (17:07-17:17) - at 17:17:00 the highest of all 21 otel-demo pods (next: postgresql 25%). Recommendation CPU usage rose from ~0.012 cores (steady 16:41-17:01) to ~0.095 cores against the 100m limit over the same minutes, with working set growing ~42 MB to ~60 MB (limit 160Mi, not near the limit). So frontend-proxy returns 504s because its upstream frontend cannot complete the recommendations call, and frontend cannot complete it because the single-replica recommendation Deployment's container CPU limit is exhausted and almost continuously throttled. No pod on that path restarted or was OOMKilled/evicted, all nodes are Ready without pressure, and every otel-demo Deployment reports 1/1 ready. What raised recommendation's CPU demand around 17:00 is not established by the available evidence.

claims.text: frontend-proxy's own 'ingress' server spans carry error status inside the authorized window: over 72m, increase(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="frontend-proxy",span_name="ingress",status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"}) = 63.98 versus 22604.77 UNSET spans. The matching client operation 'router frontend egress' shows 0 error spans in the status_code series, although individual spans of that operation do carry error="true" tags.

The frontend-proxy error spans are HTTP 504 with durations of ~15.00 s (e.g. ingress span 6b4571fe1450a2e5: 15,001,799 us, status_tags {error=true, http.status_code="504", otel.status_code="ERROR"}; its child 'router frontend egress' span 7feb370bdbad2376: 15,001,396 us, error="true", http.status_code="0"). The same 15 s/504 pattern repeats across the sampled error spans between 17:06:55 and 17:11:10, and every matching load-generator 'GET' span also reports http.status_code 504.

frontend-proxy ingress error volume grew from a low baseline into the alert level: increase over 10m of the error spans was 0 up to 16:47, 1.15 at 16:49 (low-level 503s such as the 16:43:30 trace with http.status_code 503), then 2.22 (17:03), 3.16 (17:05), 8.42 (17:09), 28.4 (17:11), 44.4 (17:13), 53.7 (17:15) - the sustained rise begins around 17:03 and the alert opens at 17:05:17.

Only the recommendations path degraded on frontend, per frontend's own span-duration p95 by span_name: 'GET /api/recommendations' and 'executing api route (pages) /api/recommendations' went 327/310/314/334/318/338/338 ms (16:50-17:02) -> 1470 ms (17:04) -> 8601 ms (17:06) -> 13098 ms (17:08) -> 15000 ms (17:10-17:16); the client span 'grpc.oteldemo.RecommendationService/ListRecommendations' followed the identical curve (172 ms baseline -> 1313 -> 8570 -> 13098 -> 15000 ms). In the same series GET / stayed 90-135 ms, GET /api/cart 151-187 ms, GET /api/data 96-223 ms, GET /api/products/{productId} 110-166 ms, POST /api/checkout 617-910 ms, and frontend's client spans to grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds, grpc.oteldemo.CartService/GetCart|AddItem and grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder remained flat.

In trace 40fc89a0cadcbbb31ce5939d98b85f7e the whole 15 s is spent waiting on the recommendation call: load-generator GET 15,003,336 us (504) -> frontend-proxy ingress 15,001,799 us (504) -> 'router frontend egress' 15,001,396 us (error=true) -> frontend 'GET' 15,001,407 us (http 200) -> 'executing api route (pages) /api/recommendations' 15,076,498 us and client span 'grpc.oteldemo.RecommendationService/ListRecommendations' 15,074,102 us, while the product-catalog spans inside the same trace are fast (oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/ListProducts 126 us, four GetProduct spans 38-2053 us, rpc.grpc.status_code 0).

The recommendation service stopped completing requests: its span counts per 5m for '/oteldemo.RecommendationService/ListRecommendations' and internal 'get_product_list' fell from 278.9/235.3/230 (16:45-16:49) to 142.2 (17:05), 27.8 (17:07) and 0 from 17:09 onward, while the frontend's 'grpc.oteldemo.RecommendationService/ListRecommendations' client span count stayed flat at ~190-275 per 5m through 17:17 (73.4 in the final partial bucket).

The recommendation pod's container is CPU-limit bound: CFS throttled-period ratio rose from 0.051-0.056 (16:41-17:01) to 0.2396 (17:03), 0.652 (17:05), then 0.964/0.968/0.958/0.969/0.968/0.996 (17:07 through 17:17), and container_cpu_usage_seconds_total rose from ~0.0122 cores (17:01) to 0.0595 (17:05) and ~0.092-0.096 cores (17:07-17:13) against the pod's 100m CPU limit.

At 17:17:00 recommendation-5f45f75855-htttv has the highest CFS-throttling ratio of all 21 otel-demo pods at 0.9965; the next highest are postgresql 0.25, cart 0.236, frontend 0.210, quote 0.156, product-catalog 0.150, currency 0.123, otel-collector 0.093, payment 0.065, ad 0.033, frontend-proxy 0.029, fraud-detection 0.023, email 0.024, shipping 0.016, valkey-cart 0.017, load-generator 0.010, and accounting/checkout/flagd/image-provider/kafka at 0.

Recommendation's working set grew from ~42.0 MB (16:41-17:01) to 54.5 MB (17:03) and ~60.0 MB (17:13-17:17) against a 160Mi memory limit, i.e. the pod is not near its memory limit; product-catalog's working set stayed ~12-13 MB throughout.

The recommendation pod was Running and Ready with 0 restarts and no previous terminated container; it was created 2026-11-16T16:23:54Z with CPU request 30m / limit 100m and memory request 80Mi / limit 160Mi. The newest recommendation log line returned was 'Receive ListRecommendations for product ids:[...]' at 2026-11-16T17:10:21.852054Z.

No Kubernetes-level failure explains the stall on this path: all 21 otel-demo pods are Running/Ready, frontend/frontend-proxy/recommendation/product-catalog show 0 restarts, all five nodes report Ready with MemoryPressure=False, DiskPressure=False, PIDPressure=False, and all 21 Deployments report 1 ready/available replica with the same 2.1.3 image digests. The only pod events returned for otel-demo concern fraud-detection.

fraud-detection changed during the window for a different reason and on a different path: container lastState.terminated.reason=OOMKilled, exitCode 137, finishedAt 2026-11-16T16:44:52Z, restarted 16:45:20Z, restartCount 3, with a kubelet 'Back-off restarting failed container fraud-detection' warning at 16:45:05Z. Its only error spans in the window are flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream spans, and it is not on the frontend->recommendation path.

product-catalog shows only a modest, later degradation of its own span p95: 1.97 ms (16:41-17:05) -> 2.03 ms (17:07) -> 3.60 ms (17:09) -> 6.08 ms (17:11) -> 7.06 ms (17:13) -> 7.13 ms (17:17), with container CPU usage 0.0024 -> 0.0077 cores over 16:41-17:01 and CFS throttling 0.150 at 17:17 against its 15m CPU limit - its rise follows recommendation's collapse rather than preceding it and is orders of magnitude smaller than the 15 s hang.

Primary: the RequestErrorRate alert on otel-demo/frontend-proxy is caused by CPU saturation of the single-replica recommendation Deployment (container recommendation, CPU limit 100m). Its container is pinned at the limit with ~96-99.6% of CFS periods throttled from 17:07 on and its own server spans stop while callers keep sending, and the resulting multi-second to >15 s ListRecommendations calls make the frontend /api/recommendations route exceed frontend-proxy's ~15 s upstream timeout, so the proxy records 504 error spans from ~17:03 onward and the alert fires at 17:05:17. The onset of the CPU demand rise (first visible in the 5m rate ending 17:03) and of the frontend latency rise (first visible in the 10m p95 ending 17:04) overlap, so the two are concurrent rather than strictly ordered, but the 99.6% throttle and the vanishing recommendation spans place the blockage inside the recommendation workload.

Secondary, unresolved: something inside the recommendation container roughly doubled its per-request CPU cost at ~17:00 (usage 0.012 -> 0.095 cores at a constant caller rate of ~46 ListRecommendations calls/min), so the pod now needs more than its 100m limit to serve the same traffic. Candidate mechanisms such as internal retry loops or heavier per-request work cannot be confirmed from the available data.

The flagd feature-flag provider is not supported as the cause: recommendation's '/flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream' error spans are only ~1.05 per 10m from 16:45 through 17:05 and fall to 0 after 17:05 (i.e. they stop before the stall peaks), the same EventStream errors appear on ad (3.05 per 72m) and fraud-detection (1.04) whose paths show no such latency degradation, and the flagd pod itself has 0 CFS throttling at 17:17.

frontend-proxy and frontend are not resource-saturated themselves: frontend-proxy reports 0.029 CFS throttling and ~0.011 cores of CPU usage (30m limit) throughout, frontend holds a steady 0.20-0.28 throttling ratio and ~0.042 cores (100m limit) with no change at the onset, and frontend's per-service error status count is 0 across 72m (98591.8 UNSET spans flagged UNSET) - so the 504s are not the proxy or frontend exhausting their own quota but 15 s upstream waits caused by the recommendation call.

Rejected: node-level resource pressure or a cluster/Deployment-level outage as the cause. All five nodes are Ready with MemoryPressure, DiskPressure, PIDPressure and NetworkUnavailable all False, and all 21 otel-demo Deployments report 1/1 ready and available with unchanged 2.1.3 image digests; only the recommendation container's own cgroup shows throttling at ~100%.

Rejected: the fraud-detection OOMKill/BackOff restart (OOMKilled exit 137 at 16:44:52Z, restarted 16:45:20Z) as the cause of this alert. It is a checkout-path dependency, frontend's grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder p95 stayed at 431-790 ms and POST /api/checkout at 617-910 ms, and the degraded path is the recommendations call whose own blocker is the throttled recommendation container.

Raise the recommendation Deployment's CPU limit (currently 100m) and/or reduce per-request work, since its single replica is pinned at 100% of its limit with ~99.6% CFS throttling; consider more than one replica so a single saturated pod cannot remove all recommendation capacity.

Have a human inspect the recommendation service internals (goroutine dump / profiler, flagd client configuration, and what changed in its workload around 17:00) to explain why CPU demand at constant request rate rose from ~0.012 to >0.1 cores, and confirm whether the service is still processing requests after its newest observed log line at 17:10:21.852054Z.

gaps: The RequestErrorRate alerting rule could not be read: list_prometheus_rules returned no rules for rule_name=RequestErrorRate and no alerting rules at all (status no_data), so the rule expression behind the annotation value 0.06666666666666667 could not be verified or re-derived.

No kube-state-metrics or kube_* series exist in this Prometheus (kube_* selector and kube_deployment_status_replicas_available returned no data), so container CPU limits/requests and historical Deployment/pod readiness could not be read from metrics; limit values came from live pod objects, whose state is the query-time state rather than the incident state.

A Jaeger search for service recommendation between 17:10:30 and 17:17:44 returned no data (status no_data), and a 5s+ duration search for that service returned none; absence of recommendation spans after 17:10 is therefore unconfirmed, and the missing recommendation spans in trace 40fc89a0cadcbbb31ce5939d98b85f7e cannot be distinguished between not-exported and not-sampled.

The recommendation pod log query filtered for err|error|fatal|timeout|fail|exception|panic|warn returned no data (status no_data) for 16:40-17:00, so the absence of recommendation-side error lines is unverified, and log lines after 17:10:21.852054Z are unknown (the returned view was limited to the newest 60 of 1584 lines).
The frontend pod log fetch for 17:05-17:17 and for 16:40-17:17 with an error filter both returned no data, so frontend-side runtime errors could not be checked at all.
The networkpolicies query for otel-demo returned no data, so the absence of NetworkPolicy objects (and any network-layer cause) is unknown rather than established.

Recommendation's CPU demand above its 100m limit is unmeasurable because the cgroup caps the reading, and no application-internal metric or profile exists for the recommendation service, so the reason for the demand rise at ~17:00 is unknown.

I did not verify that every frontend-proxy 504 in the window belongs to the /api/recommendations route; the sampled 504 traces all did and frontend's span-level p95 degrades only on that route, but an exhaustive per-route error breakdown is unavailable in this sampled trace data.
Pod logs only cover what the node still keeps and the recommendation container has no previous instance, so no pre-restart logs exist to compare; there was in any case no restart to compare against.
The change_history integration is not available in this Run, so no deployment, config or feature-flag change history could be checked for the ~17:00 onset.
Whether recommendation's memory growth from ~42 MB to ~60 MB is a cause or an effect of queued requests is not established; it remains well below the 160Mi limit.
next_steps: Compare the recommendation Deployment's per-request CPU cost and replica count with observed load (~46 ListRecommendations calls/min) and raise the 100m CPU limit or add replicas if this rate is expected to persist.
Capture a goroutine/CPU profile from recommendation-5f45f75855-htttv and confirm whether its request throughput recovers when its CPU limit is raised or the pod is recreated.
Review the flagd evaluation path in the recommendation service and the ~1 per 10m EventStream disconnects seen on ad, fraud-detection and recommendation for any retry amplification.
Separately review fraud-detection, which was OOMKilled (exit 137) at 16:44:52Z and restarted to restartCount 3, as an unrelated reliability issue on the checkout path.
Check whether frontend-proxy's ~15 s upstream/route timeout and retry settings are appropriate for the recommendations route, since the observed 504 durations match that timeout exactly.
